races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Rated Race

runners_data.name: La Tache
runners_data.note: Won over this 5f trip on Good ground on last run, with all three career starts on similar going (3/3 sim-going record) and a stable in flying form (T14: 7/31); Colin Keane takes over, and dropping back to 5f from 6f is a clear positive — a prominent racer who should get a clear run in second or third.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having been fourth two starts back and sixth three back, and quick to race again just five days later. Has run over today's trip and going before, though only fourth of eight on our figures at 138lb.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's OR 120 inmate is the only confirmed front-runner and should find life easy in the lead without a challenger; 34 days off and a form line of 1-3-0 shows a winner who has since disappointed, so the bounce risk is real — Dylan Browne McMonagle will need to judge the gallop perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back and a third two back headline a strong recent sequence, with the trainer red-hot at 19 from 59 (32%) lately. Rated the best of this field on our figures, having raced over today's trip and going before, aside from a blank last time out.

runners_data.name: Grayrobin
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 5f Good and then stepped up to 6f and found it a step too far (8th); Kate McGivern's yard has just a 2-runner 14-day record and minimal market presence, but the form reversal back to 5f is the key angle, and Chris Hayes is a reliable partner for a horse who showed real early zip on debut.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having been eighth previously. Has run over today's trip before and returns after 22 days, but sits only sixth of eight on our figures from 133lb at stall one.

runners_data.name: Sirocco Sands
runners_data.note: Dropped in trip to 5f last time and won on Soft, but all three sim-going efforts are on Good or Good to Firm (1W1P); a natural front-runner by style whose chance is tempered by the reality that Star Prospect will take the lead, leaving Luke McAteer to decide whether to fight for position or drop in — that tactical dilemma is a genuine concern.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, fourth two starts back, and second three starts back, form that stacks up well. Has run over today's trip before and sits third of eight on our figures at 133lb, though a 27-day break is the one query.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce takes a 3lb claim and the horse does have a win over 5f (Heavy), but four of five career runs have come over 6f and the form string (4-1-5-3-4) is inconsistent; naturally prominent in style, he will likely be shuffled back as the field jostles early, and the 5d turnaround from his last run adds a small fitness question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Lars Soldier has won once in his last five and is quick back just five days on, a fourth last time and a third before that keeping him competitive. Rated our second of eight and having raced over today trip and going, he is a leading danger, if one whose form has cooled a touch.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan is always worth respecting tactically and the stable has a small but active record, but this filly's form figures of 6-10-6-3-2 show a hold-up type that has struggled on Good or Good to Firm ground (0 wins, 0 places in 2 sim-going starts); 5f with a controlled pace is structurally against her true running style.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, with a third four starts back and a second five starts back preceding a below-par sixth last time out. Has raced over today's trip and going before, though only fifth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's juvenile carries a 7lb claim for Jessica Maye and arrives on a form line of 2-7-8 with her only placed effort coming on Soft — the two Good-ground runs have yielded 7th and 8th; a true hold-up profile in a pace-controlled race on fast ground makes this a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last three starts and the trainer is out of form at 0 from 28 in the past fortnight. A second three starts back is the highlight, but this sits seventh of eight on our figures despite experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Hi Corbett Court
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey's gelding is equipped with a tongue-tie and showed promise with a 3rd last time over 6f Good, but the step down to 5f is unproven and both career starts have come over 6f; a hold-up racer by style, W J Lee will need a strong pace to materialise that simply may not arrive in this configuration.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last two starts, unplaced last time out having finished third two starts back. Has run over today's trip before, but bottom of the rankings on our figures at 123lb, and a 28-day gap since that run adds to the questions.

races.paceDynamic: Star Prospect is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an eight-runner 5f field on Good to Firm ground at Cork, the tempo is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than searingly contested. Grayrobin and La Tache will press from prominent berths but neither is a natural pace-maker, meaning Star Prospect can dictate terms and avoid a war for the lead. This race shape — a single leader setting a measured gallop on fast ground over a sharp five furlongs — strongly favours prominent and close-tracking profiles that can sit just behind the early pace and pounce in the final furlong, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into. The field holds more prominent types than the race can comfortably accommodate: Sirocco Sands and Lars Soldier are genuine prominent racers mapped to midfield due to congestion, and Star Prospect alongside Grayrobin are best placed to actually secure their preferred positions at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect dictates a measured gallop and the prominent horses track closely before a sprint finish develops.
scenarios.body: Star Prospect sets a sustainable tempo on the Good to Firm ground, and the runners sitting just behind — Grayrobin and La Tache — are perfectly positioned to launch their challenges in the final furlong without having wasted energy fighting for position. This scenario rewards horses that break cleanly, travel with cover close to the pace, and possess a sharp turn of foot over the last 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect settles comfortably in front, the pace is genuinely moderate, and no rival lands a telling blow from behind.
scenarios.body: With the pack fragmented in pursuit and no horse able to close the gap on a fast surface that rewards early position, Star Prospect's class advantage (OR 120) becomes decisive as those tracking wide or out of position fail to reel it in. A flat-out sprint from the front suits a juvenile that has already won over this trip and surface condition.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect goes too fast early and ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for runners coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Lars Soldier or Sirocco Sands, despite being mapped to midfield due to overcrowding of prominent types, could still be travelling strongly if they settle slightly further back than ideal and benefit from a weakening leader. The fast ground does not typically encourage dramatic late surges over 5f at Cork, limiting the scope of this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, leaving Hi Corbett Court, Celestial Crown or Belle Island with ground to make up in the final stages.
scenarios.body: Hi Corbett Court showed a placed effort last time and Wayne Lordan aboard Belle Island provides a strong tactical hand, but true hold-up profiles face a structural disadvantage in a single-paced 5f where the leader controls the fractions. Celestial Crown, fitted with no headgear and carrying a 7lb claim, lacks the form figures to suggest she can make up sufficient ground from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Star Prospect's gallop fractions are the engine of this entire race — if Dylan Browne McMonagle sends it clear unchallenged, the race shape will be decided inside the first furlong and prominent rivals must react immediately or lose all chance.

Sirocco Sands and Lars Soldier are both natural prominent types who cannot both get their preferred berth; watch the first two furlongs for crowding on the stands rail — any bumping or shuffling back will significantly reduce their chances.

La Tache's last run was just five days ago and she steps back to a shorter trip; if there is any residual stiffness or she fails to stride out freely in the early stages, Colin Keane may find himself further back than ideal given the controlled pace.

Hi Corbett Court's tongue-tie is noted on only his second career start — if it aids him in settling better and traveling more smoothly than his debut suggests, W J Lee could find himself in a better tactical position than his hold-up tag implies, but he still needs pace to close into.

races.name: Doneraile Handicap

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here with recent course-and-distance wins and strong good-going form (14/15 sim-going entries at par or better); Chris Hayes takes the ride and will look to exploit a clear lead, though the STYLE_FIT tag suggests this OR-102 horse is racing slightly out of its most comfortable role and may not have the tactical reserves to repel a late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and again five back, with a below-par ninth last time out the exception. Quick to run again six days on and has raced over today's trip and going before, form solid enough to make it the choice here.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer fresh from two wins in recent starts including a 5f good-ground victory just 2 days ago, which demands close fitness scrutiny; Denis Hogan's 2-from-27 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's profile — quick returns, upward form, comfortable at this trip — keeps it firmly in the picture.
runners_data.comment: Won three and four starts back but has since faded to sixth last time out, a mixed recent slate. Quick to run again after just two days and has raced over today's trip and going before, though only seventh of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up specialist who is a natural wait-and-pounce type, with three places from 5f good-ground runs and tongue-tie and visor headgear suggesting connections are working hard to sharpen focus; the 26-day break is manageable and Gary Carroll gives it professional handling, but the horse needs something to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last six but boasts thirds two and three starts back and tops the rankings in this field of eleven. Has raced over today's trip and going before, though a 26-day gap since that run is the main query.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old prominent racer who has a 5f good-going win in recent form and benefits from G M Lyons' yard in superb current nick (7/31 in 14 days); Nicola Burns claims 5lb and the lighter weight helps, though the horse has also placed over 6f which suggests it stays this trip well rather than just blasting early.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back but well below that with an eighth last time out, form that swings widely. Has run over today's trip before and sits fourth of eleven on our figures, a solid enough standing to feature strongly.

runners_data.name: Chicago Call
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has been competitive in good-ground 6f handicaps and has a second over that trip in similar conditions; the 68-day layoff is the most significant concern here — the longest absence in the field — and while Coen is a strong booking, this horse needs the race to genuinely fall apart up front to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five, a second five starts back the highlight. Trainer out of form (0 from 28) and a first run in 68 days, though it has raced over today's trip before and sits fifth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with a recent 5f good-ground placed run, but displaced to a midfield mapping because the prominent berth is already overcrowded; the tongue-tie and cheekpieces headgear combination shows connections are trying to sharpen it, and the 7-apprentice claim helps with weight, but this horse will burn energy getting position it may not secure.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five, but was runner-up last time out and five starts back either side of a flat middle spell. Has raced over today's trip and going before and sits sixth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's booking on Patrick Magee's 4-from-14 14-day team is one of the stronger trainer-jockey angles in this race; a 5f good-going winner in recent form, Rosie Frith is one of the legitimate prominent racers with every right to a front-rank position and, if it travels cleanly in behind Kendall Roy, becomes a serious finisher.
runners_data.comment: Won two and five starts back but has been unplaced and eighth in between, a genuinely mixed record. Fourth last time out, has raced over today's trip and going before, and sits eighth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old whose natural racing style is to race prominently but will be pushed into midfield by the volume of pace-setters in this field; recent form shows a 2nd over 6f on fibresand and solid good-going placings, but Donagh O'Connor will have to manage an unfamiliar position, and the style-fit discount is meaningful over this sharp 5f.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five, but ranks third of eleven on our figures and was runner-up five starts back. Quick to run again just six days on and has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the redistributed prominent types — two wins from 5f good-going runs and the trainer has hit 3-from-12 in the last 14 days; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and the horse genuinely wants to be forward, but squeezed into a midfield role by the field's pace profile it will need a cleaner run than its mapped position suggests.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out with two wins in its last six, including one two starts back. Has raced over today's trip and going before and is quick to run again just six days on, though ranked only ninth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose best win came over 5f on soft at a younger age and whose recent record on good ground at this trip is limited to minor placings; the 27-day gap is standard and Marnane's yard has had two recent winners, but this horse needs everything to go right in a race that may not truly fall apart.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out but with two wins across its last six starts, three and five back, and a second six back among a solid slate. Has run over today's trip before, though rated only tenth of eleven in this field, leaving it needing more to feature.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: A prominent racer by nature who finished 2nd over 5f good-going relatively recently, but like the other redistributed types faces the real prospect of racing outside its comfort zone; Rebecca Parsons claims 10lb which is the biggest allowance in the field, providing a weight edge that partially offsets the positional disadvantage, though the sim-going record (4/11) is the weakest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, a second three starts back the standout in an otherwise modest sequence that also includes a ninth and an unplaced effort. Has raced over today's trip and going before, but sits bottom of the field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Kendall Roy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected to materialise immediately, is likely to dictate at a controlled but honest clip on good-to-firm ground — a surface that rewards horses who travel fluently and don't expend energy fighting for position. Sarahmae, Howd'yadoit, and Rosie Frith are the legitimate prominent racers likely to slot in behind the leader, with Colin Keane aboard Rosie Frith and Chris Hayes on the front-running Kendall Roy providing strong positional jockey influence. The field is loaded with natural front-runners — Eclairage, Ipanema Queen, Genesis, and Fox In Flight are all true prominent types who will be unable to secure their preferred position and are mapped to midfield as a consequence, meaning the early portions of this race will see competition for that prominent berth before the field settles. On a flat 5f in good-to-firm conditions with a sustainable pace from the front, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently without burning themselves out — specifically those with genuine positional claims in the first rank rather than the redistributed types who will find themselves further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kendall Roy Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Kendall Roy dictates from the front without significant pressure and the prominent horses behind settle into rhythm.
scenarios.body: Kendall Roy leads at a sustainable gallop, the true prominent racers — Sarahmae and Rosie Frith — track in second and third, and the race develops into a test of who can sustain their early position into the final furlong; on good-to-firm ground over 5f the leader earns a significant advantage by avoiding early energy battles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Edges It
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine prominent racers — Sarahmae, Howd'yadoit, or Rosie Frith — get a clean position early and outstay the leader in the final 1f.
scenarios.body: Kendall Roy sets the pace but is challenged by two or three natural prominent types from the 2f pole, and the sustained gallop on quick ground turns it into a flat-out sprint finish that suits those who have tracked with cover rather than led; Sarahmae's recent form and Howd'yadoit's trainer's 7-from-31 strike rate in a 14-day window add meaningful support.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected — multiple prominent types fighting for position — and the hold-up horses benefit from a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: Erosandpsyche or Chicago Call, genuine hold-up types who have the tactical patience to wait for gaps, benefit if the race ignites quickly and the leaders run into a wall inside the final furlong; Chicago Call has strong good-going form and Erosandpsyche has placed three times at this trip and going combination, giving both credible closing claims.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Beats Map
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-pressed prominent horses — Eclairage, Genesis, or Fox In Flight — manages to secure a better position than their mapped midfield slot and travels into contention.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability shape precisely because those horses are displaced by a crowded prominent berth and will likely expend energy fighting for position rather than conserving it; Genesis has the best recent form of the group and the smallest field gap to overcome, but the style-fit discount is real.

watchPoints.text: Rosie Frith to be tracked from the gates — if Colin Keane secures the prime prominent slot directly behind Kendall Roy without burning energy, the horse's good-to-firm 5f form makes it a principal danger to the leader.

Watch for early position chaos between Eclairage, Genesis, Ipanema Queen, and Fox In Flight — all four are natural prominent types who cannot all get their spot, and any pushing-and-shoving in the first furlong could compromise multiple runners and compress the race shape.

Chicago Call's 68-day absence is the longest in the field; if the horse is ring-rusty it will not get competitive at the top of the straight and Ben Coen may find there is simply no late sprint available after a break of that length on quick ground.

Kendall Roy's STYLE_FIT tag is worth monitoring in-running — if the horse appears to be straining to hold its position rather than relaxed on the front, the prominent pack tracking behind may close faster than the market implies in the final 1f.

Genesis's trainer (3/12 last 14 days) and Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim make this one of the better-value watch angles among the redistributed runners — if it does manage to slot into a prominent position early rather than its mapped midfield slot, reassess its live chances immediately.

races.name: Follow Us On Social Media Handicap

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose form figures 068000 and a tendency to fade late are deeply uninspiring; four of five recent runs on similar going yielded no placed finish, and the Denis Hogan yard is 2/27 in the past fortnight, giving little confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts but rated third of 21, boosted by a strong 66 speed figure. Carries 142 lb from stall 10 and has run over today's trip and going before. Freshened 15 days, though modest finishes leave the leading show still awaited.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner who can control fractions uncontested, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that this nominal prominent tag is racing slightly out of role on the pace map; has four recent runs over this exact track and trip, going 1W on Good, so course form is genuine but finishing record suggests he gets caught late.
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back headlines the form, backed by a 4th last time out. Top-rated on a strong 73 speed figure, with experience over today's trip and going. Back in action just 13 days on, with only a blank two starts back to note.

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for W P Browne whose last five runs have all come over 5f on slower ground than today; stepping to 6f on good-to-firm at Cork looks a significant ask, and the 0W0P sim-going record over comparable conditions is a red flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts but rated fourth of 21 with a useful 65 speed figure. Has run over today's distance before. A run of finishes no better than 5th, his latest 20 days ago, is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed three times in fifteen runs on similar going and ran third over 6f at Heather recently; the 42-day break is a slight concern but Charles Weld runners often reappear fresh, and McGettigan's 5lb claim is a useful weight relief.
runners_data.comment: A 3rd five starts back is the highlight of a mixed campaign, backed by a strong 72 speed figure that puts her second of 21 here. Winless since, including a 7th last time out, 42 days ago. Has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: El Fontenaro
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with four placings from eleven runs on similar going, including two second-place finishes over 6f on Good in recent form; Ronan Whelan is a strong booking for this yard and the horse's 6f Cork track bias is a real asset on this card.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back runner-up finishes catch the eye, backed by a strong 79 speed figure. Yet to convert those placings into a win, with a 6th and an unplaced run further back in the book. Has run over today's trip and going before, quick to return 13 days on.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Busy prominent-style performer on good ground who has finished in the first three in four of his last five runs over 5-6f on Good; DBM takes the ride, a significant jockey upgrade, and the very recent run (7 days ago) suggests peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts but consistent, with two thirds and a 2nd among his recent efforts. A fair 70 speed figure and a quick 7-day turnaround are in his favour. Rated only 13th of 21 here, having run over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse over longer trips — historic form over 8-10f — pushed into the midfield on the map as the rear is overcrowded; the fade-in-finish flag and 0W0P record on comparable going make it hard to be enthusiastic at OR=50 in this sharp 6f scramble.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts and yet to threaten the frame, with an 8th his best recent finish. Back within 12 days of his last run, he has run over today's distance before. Rated 8th of 21, on a modest 57 speed figure.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is compromised by the field's depth; has shown ability over 5-6f on Good (3rd and 5th in recent outings) but the 7lb claimer Tormey and a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 mean this only makes appeal if closers land a rare late blow.
runners_data.comment: Two thirds five and six starts back show his level, though his last two runs have both been 8th. A fair 70 speed figure and experience over today's distance keep him in this. Winless in six starts, with a 30-day break since his latest run the concern.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Most interesting of the hold-up horses — has an actual win over 5f on Good at OR=50 in recent form and Robert Whearty rides; the 6f trip is slightly longer than ideal but the horse is proven in similar conditions and represents the best closer's chance if the pace collapses late.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight of a mixed campaign, backed by a useful 75 speed figure. Has run over today's trip and going before. A 5th last time out leaves her rated 12th of 21 here.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old with a fade-in-finish warning and a moderate sim-going record (0W1P from nine runs); finished third over 6f Good recently but has also thrown in several double-digit efforts on this track and trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts, with a 3rd three starts back the highlight, though a 9th last time out is more typical of late form. A modest 56 speed figure and experience over today's distance are in his favour. Rated 5th of 21.

runners_data.name: Alandownunder
runners_data.note: Consistent midfield-to-rear type who drops in trip from 7-8f to 6f, which may bring improvement, but all five recent runs have ended outside the places on Good ground and the fade flag is concerning at OR=52.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts with three finishes of 9th among her recent efforts, a sign of a stiff task. A fair 66 speed figure and experience over today's distance are the plus points. Rated 11th of 21, back 24 days after her last run.

runners_data.name: The Cosy Corner
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner for Patrick Magee (4/14 last 14 days — a live trainer stat) but four runs on Good have returned 0W0P and the fade tendency makes the straight at Cork problematic without a strong pace to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts with only a 9th to show as a best finish, leaving plenty to prove. A modest 60 speed figure and experience over today's distance are the only real positives. Rated 14th of 21, quick to return just 13 days after her last run.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader at OR=51 trained by Miss Natalia Lupini; Colin Keane's booking is the headline angle here, but the form figures 89-004 on similar going and a fade flag make it hard to construct a winning case without a significant improvement in trip efficiency.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts and hard to fancy on our figures at 15th of 21, though a 4th last time out is a point in his favour. Finishes of 9th and 8th sit among mostly below-the-frame efforts. Has run over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Auguste Gusteau
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old — just four runs — whose hold-up style has been redistributed to midfield; all seven placings on similar going are outside the frame and Ben Coen, while a fine jockey, has limited material to work with based on the bare form at OR=50.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts and rated only 19th of 21. A 7th last time out continues a run of finishes outside the frame, with a 6th four starts back his best effort. Has run over today's distance before, back 16 days after that run.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win at OR=50 on Good, but the fade-in-finish flag and redistribution note mean this is not a true hold-up position today; W J Lee is a strong jockey booking but the 14 runs on similar going return only 1W1P and the 6f trip has been a graveyard for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts, with a 4th the best of a mixed campaign, though more recent form (two 8ths and two unplaced runs) is modest. A fair 64 speed figure keeps her in this, and she has run over today's distance before. Rated 10th of 21.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Banter
runners_data.note: Prominent type dropping sharply to OR=45 for Andrew Slattery (4/39 last 14 days); finished second over 6f recently and has multiple placed efforts at this trip, and with the senior trainer taking the ride himself, yard confidence may be present.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts but a 2nd three starts back shows ability, backed by a useful 68 speed figure. Has run over today's trip and going before. His last two runs have both been unplaced, leaving him rated 9th of 21.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose redistribution to midfield is particularly damaging — true rear-of-field type whose recent form over 5-8f on Good (all double-digit finishes) and 42-day absence make this a very tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts with only a 9th to show as a recent finish, rated just 16th of 21 here. Has run over today's trip and going before. A 42-day break since her last run and a modest 58 speed figure add to the questions.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the McCreery yard (2/21 last 14 days) who has placed in good company over 5-6f on Good before; the redistribution forces a compromise position and 0W0P on sim-going in six tries limits optimism, though the 5f win pedigree means the sharp end of 6f is not impossible.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts and rated only 17th of 21, with a 5th three starts back his sole finish inside the top half. A fair 68 speed figure and quick 7-day turnaround are the plus points. Has run over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Ballerina Dancer
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up fader who has raced just three times — all outside the places over 7-8f on Good or Soft; stepping down to 6f and facing 20 rivals is a steep learning curve, and the 53-day layoff adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in three starts and rated bottom of the field at 21st, with only a 9th the best of a modest book. A low 44 speed figure reflects that level, and she returns after a 53-day break. Hard to make a case for her on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: Another lightly-raced three-year-old (three runs, all zero-placings over 6-10f on Good) who is redistributed to midfield despite a true hold-up style; nothing in the bare form suggests she can compete at this level on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in three starts and rated 20th of 21, with no finish inside the frame in that spell. A low 44 speed figure underlines the modest level, though he has run over today's distance before. Back 30 days after his last run, this looks a tough task.

runners_data.name: You Smiled
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader with four runs all finishing outside the places over 5-6f on Good and Soft; a trainer-jockey combination (Slattery riding for himself, 4/39 yard) that occasionally fires a market mover, but the form figures 9070 make this a speculative proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts and rated 18th of 21, with a 7th two starts back her best recent finish. Has run over today's distance before, though the modest 57 speed figure caps her claims. Back 21 days after her last run.

races.paceDynamic: I'm Spartacus is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field over 6f at Cork on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Adam Caffrey can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any pressure forcing the tempo through the first half. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Love Bomb, Jazzit, Captain Ciano, Auguste Gusteau, Snowballs and others — but the pace map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and several will be forced to race closer than ideal, creating a bunched midfield rather than a truly strung-out field. El Fontenaro, Whatswrongnow and Rosato are the most likely prominent types to secure natural positions just behind the leader, giving them a clean passage against the rail or down the middle. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace — they will travel into the race without burning energy, find daylight early in the straight, and have first run on the hold-up horses who must come from further back in a compressed field with little room to manoeuvre.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus sets an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent horses slot in cleanly behind.
scenarios.body: I'm Spartacus dictates the fractions unchallenged and the race develops into a sustained 2f duel from the home bend, favouring those who have tracked the pace throughout; El Fontenaro and Whatswrongnow are ideally placed to challenge first with a clear run, having the fitness and course form to last home on this ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the leader kicks early, compressing the race into a sprint finish in which prominent types have the positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace followed by a sudden injection of pace from the front two furlongs out suits those who have sat just behind the leader and can respond immediately; Rosato has the course and distance form at a lenient mark, and Whatswrongnow's recent 6f good-ground form makes it dangerous in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late-Finishing Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and the front-runners tie up in the final furlong, leaving a gap for a closer who has been produced with a late run.
scenarios.body: This is the scenario that benefits Platino Bianco, who has won over 5f on good ground at OR=50 and can produce a powerful late effort if a gap appears; Snowballs and Jazzit are capable of finishing strongly but are racing partially out of their preferred position, reducing the probability of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes trouble in running, checks and shuffling back, creating a race where only a horse with an uninterrupted run survives.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners over 6f, interference in the early stages could cause bunching and checks that eliminate hold-up horses entirely, leaving only those with early position to benefit; Whatswrongnow and El Fontenaro, with bang-up-to-date form and prominent styles on good ground, are best equipped to avoid trouble and capitalise.

watchPoints.text: El Fontenaro and Whatswrongnow are on a collision course for the prominent positions directly behind I'm Spartacus — watch which one secures the cleaner rail berth out of the gates, as that horse gets first run in the straight.

The 21-runner field creates significant early congestion risk — hold-up horses like Jazzit, Captain Ciano and Love Bomb are likely to be shuffled even further back than intended, meaning their finishing efforts will be launched from further off the pace than their STYLE_FIT flags already suggest.
The Cosy Corner's trainer Patrick Magee is 4/14 in the last 14 days — a live stable indicator that warrants monitoring for any market support, even though the bare form is uninspiring.

Sovereign Banter drops to OR=45 with trainer Andrew Slattery riding himself — trainer-jockey combinations in Irish handicaps at this level often signal stable confidence; watch the market for unusual support given the yard's 4/39 recent strike rate.

Going is reported Good To Firm for all 6f races on the card today, firmer than the declared Good — any horses with headgear changes (Billboa: tongue-tie/bit; Heart Of Eternity: hood; Captain Ciano: hood; Hastily: hood) should be noted as connections have made interventions that may be going-related or freshness-related.

runners_data.name: Alphonsus Liguori
runners_data.note: Has the strongest recent form in the field with a win and a place over 8f on good and soft ground, and with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard for the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard, this horse sets the pace from the front — the 73-day absence is the only concern, but the talent is clear.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, following a promising 2nd before that, and rated top of this field on a strong 84 speed figure. The stable is in good form too, on a 32% strike rate over the last fortnight. A 73-day layoff is the only query.

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: Trainer Robson De Aguiar has a modest 2/16 strike rate in the past 14 days and this horse's recent string of finishes (5-3-5-5-0-9) offers little encouragement; a genuine hold-up runner by nature, it is squeezed into a more prominent role by the race shape, which works against its preferred waiting tactics.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts but a clear second here on a strong 76 speed figure, with a 3rd five starts back the standout finish and three runs of 5th further supporting the case. Has run over today's distance before, back just 12 days on.

runners_data.name: Holy Lettuce
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run to judge, a fifth over 8f on good ground, but the K.J. Condon stable has been ticking over and W.J. Lee is a reliable booking — the step down to a mile on faster ground is an open question for a horse with no exposed form to calibrate against.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced with just one start to his name, a 5th on that sole outing. Rated third of five here, though a modest 50 speed figure leaves questions over whether he can trouble the front two. Has run over today's distance before, and returns quickly, just 9 days on.

runners_data.name: The Monday Club
runners_data.note: Last seen finishing fifth over 10f on good going, which suggests this trip of a mile may be more suitable, but Diego Lima rides for a trainer with no wins from four in the past fortnight; a natural hold-up horse who will end up closer to the pace than preferred in this small field.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced with just a single start under his belt, a 5th on that occasion. Rated fourth of five here, with a fair 60 speed figure the main point in his favour. A 32-day break since that run adds to the uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Lady In The Gods
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes and finished last of 14 on good ground last time, a record that is hard to ignore; Robbie Colgan cannot disguise the lack of form, and a hold-up style combined with a tendency to weaken means this race shape offers her the least favourable canvas.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed with just a single start to her name so far, finishing unplaced on that sole outing. Too little evidence to draw firm conclusions, though she is open to improvement with more experience. A 42-day gap since that run means this represents another step into the unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Alphonsus Liguori is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over a mile at Cork. The three hold-up types — Fate's Gambit, The Monday Club, and Lady In The Gods — will be forced to track closer than their natural style dictates, compressing the field behind a single pace-setter and removing the true waiting game they prefer. Holy Lettuce is an unknown quantity stylistically, adding a degree of uncertainty to how the mid-race positions settle. This race shape heavily favours a horse who can sit just off Alphonsus Liguori's uncontested lead and pounce when the pace is wound up in the final two furlongs — a prominent, close-tracking profile is the primary beneficiary, with genuine deep closers at a structural disadvantage because they will be unable to find their natural rhythm at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alphonsus Liguori Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Alphonsus Liguori sets a controlled, unchallenged pace and the small field fails to produce a strong mid-race surge.
scenarios.body: Alphonsus Liguori bowls along in front on a sound surface that suits his form profile, and with no rival willing or able to pressure him, he converts his positional advantage into a winning lead entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a rival tracks Alphonsus Liguori close enough to strike before the final furlong without getting outsprinted.
scenarios.body: The slow early tempo invites a horse to close up travelling strongly at the halfway point and challenge as Alphonsus Liguori ties up, rewarding any runner with enough class to bridge the gap in the straight on good-to-firm ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the compressed hold-up runners find an unexpected run of daylight.
scenarios.body: With a small field on a flat, fair track, any dramatic fade from the leader opens a brief window for Fate's Gambit or The Monday Club to finish with purpose, though both are racing closer than ideal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically and a rank outsider takes advantage of the chaos created by unsettled positioning.
scenarios.body: Lady In The Gods or Fate's Gambit benefit from a messy pace scenario that nullifies Alphonsus Liguori's strengths, though poor recent form and fitness concerns make this the least credible outcome.

watchPoints.text: Alphonsus Liguori's 73-day absence is the primary risk factor — watch for any signs of rustiness in the parade ring or early in the race that could undermine his ability to maintain the front-running role he relies upon.

Holy Lettuce is lightly raced and entirely unexposed at this trip — if W.J. Lee decides to track Alphonsus Liguori closely from the outset, this horse could prove a live threat if its single run understated its ability.

The Monday Club and Fate's Gambit are both natural hold-up horses forced to race closer than ideal in a five-runner field — watch whether they settle or race keenly in the unfamiliar stalking position, as either outcome changes the closing pace dynamic.

Lady In The Gods has a noted tendency to fade in the finish and her trainer has only one runner in the past 14 days — if she shows any early reluctance or trails from the break, she will likely be a non-factor well before the straight.

races.name: Racing Again August 3rd Handicap

runners_data.name: Nathema
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up type for Andrew Slattery who has run only three times and faded on each occasion, with a 90-day absence and no win or place on similar going making this a speculative reappearance over an extended trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a fourth the best of them. She has run over today's trip before but returns from a 90-day layoff carrying 140 lb, leaving plenty to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on this hold-up performer who placed 2nd over 12f on good ground and has the most relevant form profile in the race, handling the trip and conditions competently; tongue-tie fitted and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.
runners_data.comment: One of the leading dangers on figures: runner-up three starts back, and fourth two starts back. He has run over today's trip before, but a below-par seventh last time out is the one query, leaving him to bounce back today.

runners_data.name: Glen Echo
runners_data.note: Front headgear (hood) fitted for Gavin Cromwell but this hold-up type has finished no better than third in five runs on good ground, including twice at this 13f trip, and carries a fading-in-finish flag that undermines confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: A modest third last time out is the pick of a mixed campaign, with the yard out of form at 2 from 44 recently. He has run over today's trip before and races again quickly, seven days on from his latest outing.

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter here, Ronan Whelan partners a horse whose prominent style is genuinely natural — three places in four good-ground outings over 10-12f support the claim — though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) notes he may be racing marginally out of his optimal tactical zone in a deeper field.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out and third again the run before that show consistent form, with a runner-up effort three starts back too. He has run over today's trip before, returns after just eleven days, and sits on top of our figures for this race.

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Cromwell fields a second runner whose true inclination is to race from the rear; mapped to midfield only because of field congestion, and with four consecutive finishes of 4th or worse on good ground, Jack Kearney faces a stiff task regardless of where this horse settles.
runners_data.comment: One of the leading dangers on figures, fourth last time out and fifth five starts back. She has run over today's trip before and returns quickly after eleven days, though the yard is currently out of form at 2 from 44.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's hold-up performer finished 2nd over 11f on good ground and the hood is fitted — the best piece of evidence in his favour — though he has faded in recent outings and a 20-day gap with a finish flag warrants caution at 1m4f.
runners_data.comment: One of the leading dangers on figures, with a runner-up effort last time out the highlight of a mixed campaign. She is back within 20 days but the inconsistency either side of that placing is the risk.

runners_data.name: Amethyst Stone
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle picks up the ride but this horse's record on good ground reads 13-9-12-6-15 over 10-12f — no wins, no places, consistently finishing in the rear third; in reality a back-of-field runner shunted into midfield on the map purely by numbers, and the fade flag compounds concern.
runners_data.comment: An outsider on our figures with a modest recent scoreline, unplaced last time out and only a sixth to show four starts back. He has run over today's trip before and returns after 21 days, needing plenty to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: A tongue-and-bit headgear combination for K J Condon's runner, but six runs without a win and a series of 8th, 8th, 9th placings on good ground make this difficult to support; in truth a hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map by redistribution, not by natural inclination.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out and the run before that too, with a ninth three starts back the clear low point. She returns quickly after ten days, and a strong speed figure hints at more in hand.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's presence is notable, and Wingit's 2nd-place finish over 13f on good ground is the key piece of form — only four days since last ran, which is aggressive, but Keane's ability to find positions in congested fields partly offsets the STYLE_FIT discount on this genuine rear-of-field type mapped to midfield.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out is the standout form line, even with a below-par run three starts back in between. She's fresh off just a four-day turnaround, giving her obvious claims on quick backup.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides a horse whose racing style is listed as unknown — the form includes a 2nd over 10f and a 3rd over 10f on good ground, providing genuine claims at this trip; if Foley can find a prominent position from an ambiguous style base, this horse has the course form to feature.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out backed up by a third five starts back, either side of some flat efforts in between. She has run over today's going before and returns after 16 days, with a notably strong speed figure catching the eye.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary partners a hold-up type who has never won and has finished 6th, 6th, 12th in recent good-ground starts; the redistribution into midfield on the map does not change the underlying picture, and a trainer with 0/4 in the 14-day window offers no additional confidence.
runners_data.comment: An outsider on our figures despite a runner-up effort last time out, with modest finishes either side of it. He returns after 11 days, and that placing is the one thing genuinely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Kuma Queen
runners_data.note: An absence of 339 days is the defining concern — Leigh Roche returns this hold-up filly to action having last run nearly a year ago, with three runs all resulting in 7th or worse on good ground and no form over this trip; placed in midfield by redistribution, not by preference.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures in this field, with only a seventh to show in her last three starts. She also returns from a near year-long absence, leaving considerable question marks over both form and fitness.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides a horse that improved to 3rd over 10f at Cork on good ground — the most relevant recent positive — and now steps up to 12f for the first time, which the breeding may handle; genuinely a hold-up type mapped to midfield by congestion, but the trainer's 0/3 in 14 days tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Low down our figures with a modest recent scoreline, though a third three starts back shows he retains some ability. He has run over today's trip before and is fresh from a run 11 days ago, but needs a lot to find here.

races.paceDynamic: Point Cartwright is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to pressure him from the outset, he should control tempo from the front on good-to-firm ground over 1m4f at Cork. The pace he sets is likely to be honest but not scorching — a single front-runner rarely over-cooks it when unopposed, meaning the race will be run at a sustainable rhythm that keeps the field compact through the early stages. With the field heavily populated by hold-up and prominent types, the midfield will be congested and many runners will find themselves unable to achieve their natural position; Guildhall Graduate, Amethyst Stone, Wingit, Tavarua, Canon Law, Kuma Queen and Cadreville are all redistributed from their true rear-of-field role into a notional midfield slot because there simply is not room for all of them to settle at the back. In a race with one honest pace-setter and a wall of closers unable to get their preferred spot, the tactical verdict is clear: the race shape most favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace in second or third, tracking Point Cartwright's controlled tempo and delivering their challenge without fighting traffic — Connecteo and Borora Aura, who can work through the field, and Point Cartwright himself, are the profiles to focus on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Point Cartwright Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Point Cartwright dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up brigade cannot get clear runs through a congested field.
scenarios.body: Point Cartwright sets a sustainable pace on good-to-firm ground and, with no rival willing to challenge him early, builds an advantage that the closers cannot fully close in time; the compact midfield creates traffic for those coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just off Point Cartwright's pace moves smoothly to challenge entering the straight and wins a two-horse battle.
scenarios.body: With the pace honest but not extreme, a prominent mover that has tracked the leader without expending energy in traffic is ideally placed to deliver a clean challenge; Connecteo and Borora Aura both have the positional awareness and recent trip experience to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns unexpectedly strong and the field fans wide in the straight, giving room to those held up rearmost.
scenarios.body: Should Point Cartwright quicken the tempo mid-race or the field string out, some of the redistributed hold-up horses might find gaps; Wingit, who ran 2nd over 13f on good ground, is the most credible beneficiary if this rare gap opens, though the STYLE_FIT discount limits confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Staying Grind Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow early then the field sprints for home, creating a stamina-sapping finish that catches out prominent types.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race that turns into a test of raw stamina over 1m4f on quick ground could expose surprising form; Cadreville improved to a third over 10f and steps up to a likely career-best trip, while Millhone placed over 11f and handles this going.

watchPoints.text: Point Cartwright is the only horse capable of controlling pace from the front — if Ronan Whelan bowls along unopposed and the midfield becomes a traffic jam, the rest of the field is racing for the places at best.

Wingit ran just four days ago and Colin Keane's eagerness to take such a quick turnaround with a genuine hold-up horse in a congested 13-runner field is worth monitoring — a short-to-medium term bounce risk exists.

Kuma Queen returns from 339 days off and is a completely unknown quantity fitness-wise; she could be significantly undercooked or, in the rare case of a perfect preparation, a sleeper — Leigh Roche's early positioning will be the tell.

The going report confirms Good to Firm throughout the evening at Cork — conditions are faster than the declared GOOD, which will shorten strides for hold-up types in a long 1m4f race and further advantage those who can travel close to Point Cartwright's pace.

Guildhall Graduate and Amethyst Stone are both Gavin Cromwell and Paul Flynn runners respectively who are in reality back-of-field types navigating a compacted midfield — watch whether their jockeys attempt to push forward early or accept the rear, as either choice carries a trade-off in this race shape.
